messages:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: P1 - latency spike affecting /v1/generate in us-west-2. Pager triggered (pagerduty#12345). Root cause unknown. Please acknowledge in-thread.
Maya: ack, I'm coming in to take the bridge. hopping on the bridge voice now.
Sam: acked. I'm secondary comms, will take customer updates unless you want me driving.
Maya: I'll drive. Sam, you take comms if you're green. liam said he's running late (~15m) in the handoff message.
Sam: i can do comms. thanks. can someone post any recent error rates or user impact?
Jess: quick check — spikes in 95p latency from 140ms -> 1.8s since 10:03 UTC, error rate steady but 5xx up from 0.1% -> 0.8%. looks like overload on inference pods.
Maya: runtime note: autoscaler didn't scale past 10 replicas. suspect throttling on node group. runbook says check nodepool, asg, and qps per worker. runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/p1-inference-latency
OpsBot: runbook snippet applied: recommended checklist posted.
Maya: Assignments: driver=Maya, comms=Sam. secondary=Jess (fallback). If Liam shows up he can take ops/infra.
Sam: copying the customer impact for public update: "Some customers may see increased latency for text generation calls in us-west-2. We're actively investigating and applying mitigations. No data loss reported." ok?
Maya: fine. also adding short-term mitigation: reduce max_concurrency on heavy routes and enable prefix KV caching for 3 high-traffic services. patch pinned model variant to quantized variant if we see memory pressure.
Jess: I'm flipping the routing rule now to reduce burst to the dedicated pool that has spare capacity. command I ran: ```bash
# scale up nodegroup and check pods
kubectl scale nodegroup inference-w1 --replicas=14 --region=us-west-2
kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | grep restart
```
Maya: thanks. Sam, start initial customer broadcast (internal template in #incidents/templates). Use UTC timestamps and call out mitigation steps. keep it short.
Sam: sending initial update now. posting to status page and major-customer list. will ping once published. :thumbsup:
Liam: sorry stuck in meeting, ETA ~12m. can take over comms after Sam if needed.
Maya: noted. coverage gap if Sam needs to step out — Jess will take comms. we need someone to monitor autoscaler metrics and node-group health continuously.
Jess: monitoring autoscaler + node metrics. if scale fails, we fallback to model variant with smaller memory footprint.
Incident Bot: :pushpin: Bridge note: driver=Maya, comms=Sam, secondary=Jess, backup=Liam. Incident ticket: INF-2026-789. Please update ticket with handoff on shift change.
Maya: plan for shift change at 18:30 UTC — I'll hand over driver to next on-call (EOW schedule) unless we drop below severity in next 30m. if not, I'll stay until stable or next oncall can relieve.
Sam: confirmed. If anything urgent happens while I'm on call, tag @eng-oncall and use PD escalation rules.
Jess: added runbook pointers to the ticket and linked logs (elk: https://elk.redwood/internal/app/kibana#/discover?_a=(query:(match:(service:(query:'inference',type:phrase)))))
Maya: final note for handoff: leave in ticket: what we tried, metrics at handoff (95p latency 1.2s, 5xx 0.5%), current replica count 14, mitigation applied: routing throttle + kv cache enabled. next driver should verify request latency and autoscaler activity for 10m post-handoff.
Sam: prepping the handoff message for next oncall, will paste into ticket and ping in #eng-oncall.
Maya: handing off in 10. if anyone has objections speak now.
Liam: no objections. thanks team.
Maya: handing off driver -> next_oncall (after shift rotate). comms -> Sam continues. logging handoff in ticket now. :white_check_mark:
